name: JaguarDB
tagline: Distributed vector database from DataJaguar that also handles time series and geospatial data.
description: JaguarDB began around 2017 as DataJaguar's distributed SQL-ish store for time series and location data and was repositioned in 2023 as a vector database for AI workloads. It indexes text and image embeddings across a multi-node cluster, keeps raw media in an 'AI datalake', and computes rolling aggregates over time windows as data arrives. Its distinctive claim is ZeroMove hashing, which lets a cluster grow without rebalancing existing data. It ships as a Docker image, Linux tarballs and an embedded variant (JaguarLite), with HTTP and socket client packages on PyPI and integrations for LangChain-style frameworks. It is a small vendor with a thin community; evaluate carefully against mainstream vector databases.

license.name: Proprietary binaries (free download); client SDKs Apache-2.0

pricing.notes: Server, cluster and JaguarLite packages are free downloads; support terms are by arrangement.

scale.notes: Vendor claims instant scale-out with no data migration via ZeroMove hashing; independent benchmarks are scarce.

strengths: Vector, time-series and geospatial data in one distributed engine
Scale-out designed to avoid data movement when nodes are added
Real-time windowed aggregates computed during ingest
Embedded JaguarLite variant for edge or single-process use
weaknesses: Small vendor; little independent documentation, benchmarks or community
Licensing of the server is not clearly published
Few managed-service options compared with mainstream vector databases
useCases: Similarity search over text and image embeddings
Combining vector search with time-series or location filters
Self-hosted RAG retrieval on Linux clusters
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a managed cloud vector service
Organisations that require a well-known vendor with SLAs
